walkthrough:
Find the median for machine A ($n = 19$ rods):
$$\text{Position of median} = \dfrac{19 + 1}{2} = 10\text{th value}$$
$$\text{Median} = 0.238\text{ m}$$

Find the lower quartile $Q_1$ and upper quartile $Q_3$:
$$\text{Position of } Q_1 = \dfrac{19 + 1}{4} = 5\text{th value} \implies Q_1 = 0.231\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_3 = \dfrac{3(19 + 1)}{4} = 15\text{th value} \implies Q_3 = 0.245\text{ m}$$

Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 0.245 - 0.231 = 0.014\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: We are given a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram showing the lengths in metres of $n = 19$ rods produced by machine A.

Step 1: Determine the median length for machine A.
With $n = 19$ ordered observations, the position of the median is:
$$\text{Median rank} = \frac{n + 1}{2} = \frac{19 + 1}{2} = 10\text{th value}$$
Counting the leaves in increasing order for machine A:
1st to 4th values: $0.220, 0.224, 0.227, 0.229$
5th to 9th values: $0.231, 0.232, 0.234, 0.235, 0.237$
10th value: $0.238$
Therefore, the median is $0.238$ m.

Step 2: Find the lower quartile $Q_1$ and upper quartile $Q_3$.
The lower half has 9 values below the median. The middle of these 9 values is the 5th value overall:
$$Q_1 = 5\text{th value} = 0.231\text{ m}$$
The upper half has 9 values above the median. The middle of these 9 values is the 15th value overall ($10 + 5$):
$$Q_3 = 15\text{th value} = 0.245\text{ m}$$

Step 3: Calculate the interquartile range (IQR):
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 0.245 - 0.231 = 0.014\text{ m}$$

hints: A complete statistical comparison requires one comment on central tendency (average length) and one comment on dispersion (spread or consistency).
Compare the medians: machine A has a higher median ($0.238$ m) than machine B ($0.232$ m), meaning machine A rods are generally longer.
Compare the spreads: machine A has a smaller interquartile range ($0.014$ m vs $0.019$ m) and range ($0.034$ m vs $0.045$ m), meaning machine A rods are less spread out and more consistent.
walkthrough:
Comparison 1 (Central tendency):
The median length of rods produced by machine A ($0.238$ m) is greater than that of machine B ($0.232$ m), showing that rods produced by machine A are generally longer.

Comparison 2 (Spread / variation):
The interquartile range for machine A ($0.014$ m) is smaller than that for machine B ($0.019$ m) (and machine A has a smaller range), showing that the lengths of rods from machine A are less spread out and more consistent.
teacher_walkthrough: We need to state two distinct comparisons in context between the rod lengths produced by machine A and machine B, using our box plots.

Rule for comparing two distributions:
Always provide:
1. One comparison of location / central tendency (medians).
2. One comparison of spread / variability (interquartile ranges or ranges).

Step 1: Compare central tendency.
Median for machine A $= 0.238$ m.
Median for machine B $= 0.232$ m.
Statement: The rods produced by machine A are generally longer than those produced by machine B (or machine A has a higher median length).

Step 2: Compare dispersion / spread.
IQR for machine A $= 0.245 - 0.231 = 0.014$ m.
IQR for machine B $= 0.243 - 0.224 = 0.019$ m.
Range for machine A $= 0.254 - 0.220 = 0.034$ m.
Range for machine B $= 0.256 - 0.211 = 0.045$ m.
Statement: The lengths of the rods produced by machine A are less spread out (more consistent) than those produced by machine B.
